note: The change ledger. These are facts about the work rather than samples, so they are committed as data and rendered into a table by analysis/reporting.mjs. 'effect' must be either a measured number with its source table, or the literal string 'not measured' - never an estimate dressed as a result.

changes.change: Recovered a per-stage profile from container logs
changes.what: The pipeline's timing decorators printed to stdout and nothing persisted them. The platform retains container stdout, so the profile was pulled back over its API from real production runs with no instrumentation change.
changes.detail: Ten stages, n=5, reconciling to the independently printed job total within 0.03 s

changes.change: Fixed the timing decorator so repeated stages accumulate
changes.what: The decorator overwrote a stage's time on each call, so any job invoking a stage more than once reported only the last invocation. Every multi-segment word-replacement job was affected.
changes.detail: Every timing table on this site flows through the fixed code path

changes.change: Pinned the dependency graph and made the image buildable
changes.what: 28 of 62 requirement lines carried no version, so every rebuild resolved a different environment and nothing had rebuilt cleanly in roughly sixteen months.
changes.detail: 221 packages pinned; first green build of the repository since May 2025

changes.change: Found and fixed a mixed-CUDA torch stack
changes.what: A version pin does not identify a build variant. Pinning torch to a version installed a CUDA 12.4 wheel from the public index, while the build's own later step installed CUDA 12.1 builds of torchaudio and torchvision. torchaudio then refuses to import, and the pipeline imports it before serving its first request.
changes.detail: The container reached a running state; a full clip completed in 398 s

changes.change: Made the sampler seedable per run
changes.what: The audio-to-expression model seeded once at construction, so the first prediction in a warm process was reproducible and every later one was not. Two runs of one clip shared zero identical frames out of 1074.
changes.detail: Prerequisite for a paired A/B, and for the cache in the same section

changes.change: Renderer batch size 4 to 16
changes.what: Roadmap item, premised on the GPU being under-fed at batch 4. Exposed as one environment variable so a single build serves both sides of the comparison.
changes.detail: -0.14% once the session drift measured by a repeated baseline is removed, and inside the output noise floor: rejected. The renderer waits on video decode, not on arithmetic

changes.change: fp16 autocast in the neural renderer
changes.what: Roadmap item. Also exposed as one environment variable, default off.
changes.detail: -0.41% drift-adjusted and inside the output noise floor: rejected as null. Its output sits no further from the baseline than a repeat of the baseline itself, so this is not a fidelity finding

changes.change: Asynchronous host-to-device transfers in the renderer
changes.what: Roadmap item, partially implemented: non_blocking on six host-to-device copies. Pinned memory already existed; CUDA streams were not built.
changes.detail: Always on, so it is inside every arm including the baseline and cannot be isolated by this design

changes.change: cuDNN autotuning scoped to the render loop
changes.what: Not a roadmap item. The animator's seeding helper disables cuDNN autotuning process-wide as a side effect, and the renderer inherits it: hundreds of convolutions at one fixed input shape, run without autotuned kernels.
changes.detail: +0.50% drift-adjusted: rejected. The raw +1.89% was almost entirely session drift, which a repeated baseline caught

changes.change: Paste-back composites only the mask bounding box
changes.what: Where the warped mask is zero the composite writes the source back over itself. Restricting it to the mask's bounding box is bit-exact by construction rather than an approximation.
changes.detail: Bit-identical across 44 cases and 400 random transforms; 1.55x to 2.90x on the function, which is about 14% of the timed stage

changes.change: Output sanity checks on every generated video
changes.what: A timing harness cannot see a black frame, a frozen output, or a face whose mouth never moves. An arm that is faster because it produced garbage would otherwise read as a win.
changes.detail: 18 of 18 A/B outputs and 16 of 16 open-dataset outputs pass. Nothing is marginal: no frozen frames anywhere, and the weakest lower-face motion is 6.7x clear of the static-mouth threshold

changes.change: Made result writes concurrency-safe
changes.what: The quality harness loaded its whole result file at start, held it for minutes, then wrote it back whole. Two concurrent scorings destroyed one another's results.
changes.detail: A completed three-clip result set was lost this way before the fix; writes now merge and rename atomically

changes.change: A baseline repeated as the last pass of the session
changes.what: Produces no information about any optimization. Its only job is to measure how much the machine itself moved between the first arm and the last.
changes.detail: +1.85% slower than the identical first pass, on the same three clips with the same seed and no code change. This is the drift correction applied to every arm above, and it is why none of them was kept

changes.change: The whole branch measured against the unmodified upstream code
changes.what: Checks the reverse risk: that the accumulated changes cost something incidental even where each was individually null.
changes.detail: -0.47% against the adjacent baseline with mixed per-clip signs, and every output inside the noise floor: the branch is performance-neutral

changes.change: Deterministic kernels behind a second flag
changes.what: Asks torch for deterministic algorithms and a fixed cuBLAS workspace on top of the reseed, to test whether the pipeline can reproduce its own output exactly. Run as two independent pairs.
changes.detail: 0 of 751 frames identical in BOTH pairs, and an 11% to 13% wall clock cost: the floor does not move, so the flag stays off. The nondeterminism sits outside torch, which is what decides the cache design

changes.change: A third baseline, with the accumulated output cleared first
changes.what: Tests whether the session drift has an avoidable cause. The pipeline writes eighteen intermediate videos per job into one directory, which had reached 20 GB. Free space was ruled out first: the volume stayed 39 % full.
changes.detail: Recovered 0.91 of the 1.85 points of drift, consistent in sign across all three clips. About the size of the 0.95% repeat CV, so it is grounds for clearing the directory between arms, not a result

changes.change: Cache the last few decoded frames in the renderer’s reader
changes.what: Not a roadmap item; it came out of the mechanism the three null arms exposed. The reader had one fast path, the next frame in sequence, while the renderer asks for five frames around each position — so every item opened with a one-frame backward step that re-decoded from the previous keyframe.
changes.detail: -14.30% and -14.76% across two independent passes 0.53% apart, all clips same direction. The neural render falls 57.9% and accounts for the whole job saving. Output-neutral on every robust statistic; still default off pending a wider validation set

changes.change: Batch the focal-length search into one solve
changes.what: The camera calibration evaluates 46 focal candidates, each a fresh 300-iteration solve on 9 KB tensors, so 14,800 iterations run one after another and never occupy the device. The candidates are independent, so they now share one solve.
changes.detail: -9.61% paired across three clips with the tracking stage down 29.8%, but that is the UNCONFIRMED variant and a ceiling. The implementation kept instead confirms the top candidates against the sequential solver, trading a 9.3x iteration reduction for 3.7x to protect exactness; that configuration is untimed and not estimated here

changes.change: Made the selected camera focal observable
changes.what: The focal is the only value the calibration sweep exports, and not one line of that module’s logging reached any run log, so no job could report what focal it chose. One print, to the stream the logs already capture.
changes.detail: It immediately showed that the sweep is not reproducible: four reads on ONE clip at ONE seed gave 2900, 1850, 1830, 1810, with all four projection errors inside 0.48% of each other. Two of those were the unmodified sequential path, at 2900 and 1830

changes.change: Reduce the parsing output on the device instead of on the host
changes.what: The stage copied a 19-class 512-square float tensor to the host per frame, about 20 MB with a blocking transfer each time, and reduced it there. Reducing first ships a single-byte class map.
changes.detail: -2.66% at the job level and -35.5% on the stage, every clip faster, bus traffic down 76x and blocking transfers from 751 to 24. REJECTED: the gate is 3% at the job level and this is 2.66%. Left rejected rather than reinterpreting the gate

changes.change: Confirmed the build fix end to end by rebuilding from the merged branch
changes.what: The deploy failure was a mixed-CUDA torch stack: PyPI's torch 2.5.1 is built against CUDA 12.4 and the index build against 12.1, and both report the same version string, so a version pin does not identify the artefact. Every run on the experiment box until now needed a --force-reinstall inside the container to obtain a consistent stack. A fresh image built from the merged branch was then inspected for what it actually contains.
changes.detail: torch 2.5.1+cu121 beside torchaudio 2.5.1+cu121 in the built image, with no runtime patching; every pip layer cached, so the resolved dependency set is now stable across builds

changes.change: Ran the two kept changes together
changes.what: They target different stages, so they ought to add — but two earlier attempts at this test were void: one passed flags to an image built before either change existed, the other set the cache to a size that misses on every frame.
changes.detail: -22.66% together, and the renderer change REPLICATED at -13.66% against -14.30% measured separately on a different image. Predicting the combined arm from the two separate experiments lands 2.24s off, 0.57% of the job and inside the run-to-run spread, so the savings add. Each change moves only its own stage

changes.change: Tested whether a second job fits on the same accelerator
changes.what: This was the largest untested lever in the work and the one the deployment arithmetic leaned on hardest: one job peaks at under half the card's memory and leaves it idle a third of the time, so a second job ought to have been nearly free. Two jobs were run in sequence, then the same two at once on the same clips at the same seed, with both kept optimizations on and the per-process memory cap lowered to 0.45 so two processes could not together claim more than the card holds. Hardware was sampled every two seconds throughout.
changes.detail: Density is WORSE, not free: total wall clock for two jobs rises from 715s to 780s, +9.1%, and throughput falls from 10.1 to 9.2 jobs per GPU-hour. Neither resource the projection reasoned about was the constraint — memory peaked at 56.7% of the card and utilization averaged 34.4% with 37.2% of samples at exactly zero. CPU cores and software video encoding bind. This retracts an earlier projection in this work that packing would roughly double throughput per card; a density test that fails because the accelerator was never scarce is direct evidence the pipeline is not accelerator-bound

changes.change: Measured keeping stage boundaries in memory instead of writing video between them
changes.what: Merged into the codebase during this work and never measured. It is the test that follows from the density result: if the binding resource is CPU-side video encoding rather than the accelerator, then the change worth trying is the one that removes encodes. Three clips, seeded, both kept optimizations on in every arm, and the treatment bracketed by two runs of the control, because a repeat of one arm earlier in this work drifted 1.85% -- larger than every effect then being chased.
changes.detail: -5.04% paired at the job level, 306.70s to 291.25s, against a drift bracket of -0.05% -- the tightest in this work, with one clip reproducing to a hundredth of a second. The effect is roughly a hundred times the bracket and clears the 3% gate. Attribution is clean and declares its own new cost: -17.57s in one stage, plus +1.94s for writing the final video once from memory at the end, reconciling with the -15.45s job delta. Counted rather than assumed, 19 intermediate video files per clip become 14, so five disappear -- a prediction of 13 was recorded before the run and was wrong, because the documentation claims six gated writes but the full-resolution paste-back video is still written in both arms. Memory: the hand arithmetic in the code, flagged there as unmeasured, is right about the sustained footprint (+2176 MiB) and wrong about the peak, which is UNCHANGED at -110 MiB, because the existing path already holds the whole source at full resolution while cropping. NOT KEPT AS OUTPUT-NEUTRAL: 9 of 9 videos pass the sanity check, but delivered pixels differ at 35.11 dB against a 40.22 dB same-configuration floor, consistently across all three clips, so this is not counted with the two bit-exact changes that shipped

changes.change: Made the video writer's frame alignment and rate control explicit, and audible
changes.what: Found by asking why the in-memory arm's output files are LARGER than the disk path's despite being smaller in both dimensions. The file that writes video contains two writers that disagree about two separate things: one passes an explicit block alignment of 2 and an explicit quality setting, and the class the pipeline actually uses passes neither, so the encoder applies its own defaults. Every frame size the pipeline computes is two pixels short of the default alignment, so every delivered video is scaled up by two pixels in each dimension and re-encoded at 55% of the bitrate the sibling writer would have used. The library does warn about the rescale, through a logging channel this application never configures for output -- zero such warnings across every run log, on a path that was rescaling every frame.
changes.detail: The default is deliberately LEFT UNCHANGED, because lowering the alignment changes the dimensions of delivered video and that is not a decision to make as a side effect of a performance change. The alignment is now configurable, and the writer announces once per file when it is about to rescale, on the same stream as the rest of the pipeline. 16 checks pin it, including the three real frame sizes observed and the requirement that the default stay as it was; one of those checks caught a defect in the announcement itself, where a bracketed prefix was being silently eaten by the terminal formatter

changes.change: Made both writers agree, and it reversed the previous row's verdict
changes.what: Row 24 concluded that keeping stage boundaries in memory could not be counted with the two bit-exact changes because it altered delivered pixels. That row also named the test that would settle it -- make the two writers agree and compare again -- and hedged instead of running it. The test took twelve minutes. Source was bind-mounted rather than rebuilt, and both knobs were verified live inside the image before launching, because an earlier arm in this work was void from passing flags to an image built before the code existed.
changes.detail: REVERSES row 24 on output. With both writer parameters set the existing path stops rescaling and writes at the same quality, and the two paths then agree at 40.19 dB against a same-configuration floor of 40.22 dB -- 0.03 dB apart. The entire earlier 5.11 dB gap was the writer's two omissions and none of it was the in-memory path, which had been measured against a reference that was damaging its own output. Speed holds: 307.69s to 290.77s, -5.50% on the one clip, consistent with the -5.04% over three clips. Against the source clip, which is the comparison both records called missing: 31.73 dB as it ships, 33.89 dB with the two writer parameters set, 34.96 dB in memory -- so the WRITER PARAMETERS ALONE are worth +2.16 dB on the shipping path at zero performance cost, and the rest of the pipeline's own run-to-run spread on this measure is 0.04 dB. The defect found while checking an optimization is worth more than the optimization

changes.change: Stopped writing per-frame tensor files that have no reachable reader
changes.what: One phase of the face-tracking stage writes two tensor files per frame into a directory named "debug". Their only reader has exactly two call sites, and neither of those functions is called from anywhere in the repository -- established by parsing the source rather than searching it, after a first attempt with a text search flagged its own documentation as a call site. The phase's consumed outputs are computed before the loop that writes the files, so skipping it cannot be observed downstream: bit-exact by construction rather than by tolerance. Default off, and the reader now raises if it is ever reached with the flag set, so reviving one of those dead functions fails loudly instead of reading files that were never written.
changes.detail: REJECTED on latency, and kept anyway on a separate claim. The writing phase drops from 3.125s to 0.041s and the enclosing stage from 104.49s to 99.65s, which is unambiguous -- that phase spanned 0.4s across three runs without the change and lands four seconds outside the band with it. But the gate is 3% at the JOB level and the job level cannot resolve this: four comparable runs without the change span 2.97% among themselves, and the treated run sits 0.59% below the fastest of them. Comparing it against the slowest control alone gives -3.05% and would read as clearing the gate; that comparison is chosen after the fact and is not quoted. What the change does deliver is 1,502 fewer files and 1,065 MB less output per job for the same 14 delivered videos -- a storage and I/O-contention argument rather than a speed one, which matters most in the case the density test exposed. Honest one-line form: frees a gigabyte per job, bit-exact, no measurable speed change

changes.change: Timed the three kinds of work inside the largest step
changes.what: It renders two meshes, copies both to the host and encodes three video streams per frame, and the split had never been measured — so the value of moving those writes into memory was unknown. Accumulators behind a flag, with a device synchronise before each clock read, and the uninstrumented function recovered by AST comparison so the measurement provably did not perturb what it measured.
changes.detail: Render 72%, encode 18%, warp 7.4%, transfer 2.5%. The obvious optimization would recover the encode share only: 1.16% of the job, not the 7.1% the step represents. Killed before it was built, for six minutes and one timer

changes.change: Measured the double encode on the preprocessing path
changes.what: The largest CPU-only item in the job prepares the source video, and it costs far more on production jobs than on the benchmark clips because production handles large customer video. Inside it, the frame-rate conversion encodes at a slow high-quality setting and the very next step re-encodes the result while passing no codec settings at all, so the encoder applies its own lower-quality defaults. The same content is encoded twice and the expensive quality is discarded before anything downstream sees it. Confirmed in the source, then measured with the encoder alone, no accelerator, three repetitions per arm.
changes.detail: Stopping the double encode is worth -51.5% of that pair. A combined -65.9% is available by also trimming in the same pass and is deliberately NOT the headline: that part depends on how much of the source the audio uses, an arbitrary ratio in this test, while encoding the same content twice is structural. Separately the discarded quality alone would cut the first pass 30.6% -- the slow setting costs 1.44x the surviving one and buys nothing that survives. Output sizes cross-check it: the fused pass lands within 1% of what the current pair produces. SCOPE: the test source is about half production resolution, so the seconds are not production figures and the result is quoted as a share of the stage; applying the ratio to the production stage cost suggests roughly 46s, and that arithmetic is derived rather than measured. NOT IMPLEMENTED -- the change is on the preprocessing path, which no arm here touched, and deserves its own before and after on a representative source
